name: Vue

hook.title: Keep your composables. Port templates when you're ready.
hook.lede: `@pyreon/vue-compat` runs the Composition API on Pyreon's engine: `ref`, `reactive`, `computed`, `watch`, the lifecycle hooks, `provide`/`inject`, `createApp`. It is a runtime layer, so components are TSX functions: `.vue` files are ported to TSX, and the composables they import keep running unchanged.

covers: `defineComponent`, `defineAsyncComponent` (loading and error components, delay, timeout), `createApp(component, props)`.
doesNotCover: The `.vue` single-file component compiler, and with it `<script setup>`.
Template directives (`v-if`, `v-for`, `v-model`): use the JSX equivalents.
Lifecycle hooks fire once per instance; `onUpdated`'s render-driven re-fires become per-subscription effects.

config.note: Aliases `vue` and its JSX runtime to the compat package.
Types and the JSX runtime come from the compat package.

ports.title: Step 1: the template becomes TSX, the logic stays

before.label: Vue single-file component
before.code:
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'

const props = defineProps<{ step: number }>()
const count = ref(0)
const doubled = computed(() => count.value * 2)
</script>

<template>
  <button class="counter" @click="count += props.step">{{ count }} / {{ doubled }}</button>
</template>

after.label: TSX on @pyreon/vue-compat

ports.note: `ref`, `computed` and `.value` are untouched; only the markup moved. Render it from a parent's JSX (`<Counter step={2} />`) so the compat runtime re-renders it.

ports.title: Step 2: refs become signals

before.label: TSX on @pyreon/vue-compat

after.label: Pyreon

ports.note: The Pyreon side is the final form, after `compat` is switched off.
